# Trimming Black or White Borders on Film Scans

Some scanners leave a thin black or white strip along one or more edges of a frame. That can be the edge of the film holder, the gap between frames, or a line the scanner draws. Left in, the strip shows up on the customer's prints and downloads.

OrderHub Desktop can find these strips for you. When it trims a frame, it:

* cuts the strip off;
* takes a little off the other sides so the frame keeps its original shape;
* enlarges the frame back to its original pixel size, so it prints at exactly the same size as before.

You can let it trim automatically, have it suggest trims for you to check, or trim any frame by hand.

---

## How it keeps your scans safe

* **It only trims automatically when it is sure.** A frame it is unsure about is never guessed at. It is either held for you to check or left untouched, depending on the option you choose.
* **The original is always kept.** The untrimmed frame stays on this PC. It is never uploaded, and **Revert to original** puts it back at any time until the roll is uploaded.
* **The shape and size don't change.** A trimmed frame has the same pixel size as before, so it prints and crops exactly as it would have.
* **Quality is kept.** Trimmed JPEG frames are saved at full quality, so they are larger files than the originals. TIFF frames stay TIFF.

---

## Turning it on

1. Open OrderHub Desktop and go to **Settings → Film Scans → Border trim**.
2. Choose an option from the **Border trim** dropdown:

| Option | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Off** | Nothing is trimmed or checked. This is the default. |
| **Suggest only — I'll check each frame** | Frames with a border are marked **Border suggested**, and nothing is changed until you accept. Doubtful frames are marked **Check border**. The roll is not held for border trim; your **Review Mode** still decides that. |
| **Trim automatically, hold doubtful frames for review** | Clear borders are trimmed automatically. If any frame is doubtful, it is marked **Check border** and the whole roll waits in the **Film Scans** tab until you approve it, even when **Review Mode** is **Auto**. |
| **Trim automatically, leave doubtful frames untouched** | Clear borders are trimmed automatically. Doubtful frames are left exactly as scanned, and the roll carries on as normal. |

3. Click **Save Settings**.

![Border Trim Options](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/231ca180-b217-4dc3-96c5-109a99e9cb29.png)

* Note: The setting applies to rolls processed after you save it. On rolls that were already processed, you can still trim frames by hand (see below).
* Note: Border trim works whether **AI Rotation** is on or off. It runs after rotation and before Perfectly Clear, so Perfectly Clear enhances the trimmed frame.

**Which option to choose?** If you're not sure, start with **Suggest only** for a few rolls. That lets you see what it finds before you let it trim on its own.

---

## Finding the frames that need you

In the **Film Scans** tab:

* **In the roll list**, choose the **Needs border check** filter to see every roll with a **Check border** or **Border suggested** frame.
* **On a roll's screen**, the chips across the top include **Trimmed**, **Check border** and **Border suggested**. Each one appears only when the roll has frames of that kind. Click a chip to show just those frames.
* **On each frame**, a badge shows **Trimmed**, **Check border** or **Border suggested**.

![Border Suggested](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/c265d32c-4d49-442f-9e21-ade6ce73e902.png)

### What the badges mean

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Trimmed** | The border has been trimmed. |
| **Border suggested** | A border was found and a trim is ready, but nothing has been changed yet (**Suggest only** mode). |
| **Check border** | There may be a border, but it isn't clear enough to trim automatically. Take a look. |

### Trimming a whole roll at once

**Trim borders on this roll** accepts every clear suggestion on the roll in one go. When it finishes, it tells you what it did, for example "Trimmed 3 frames · 1 doubtful, left for you". Click the message to jump straight to the doubtful frames.

It leaves these frames alone:

* frames already trimmed;
* frames enhanced with Perfectly Clear;
* frames you have already said not to trim.

---

## Checking and trimming a frame

Click any frame to open it in the frame viewer.

### Seeing the border

On a **Border suggested** or **Check border** frame, the area that would be removed is shaded on the picture. A key in the corner explains the colours:

| Colour | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Red** — Border (cut off) | The border itself, which will be removed. |
| **Amber** — Keeping shape | A little extra taken off the opposite sides so the frame keeps its shape. |
| **Dashed amber** — Possible border | Something that might be a border but isn't clear enough to trim. |
| **Dashed white outline** | What will be kept. |

![Border Color Meaning](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/c310e72f-a939-4279-abd7-144b7cf29b22.png)

Very thin borders are drawn a little thicker so you can see them. To see the real edge:

* click **Zoom to border**, and use **‹ Previous edge** / **Next edge ›** to step between edges; or
* click the shaded area itself.

Both show that edge at 100%. Click again, or press **Esc**, to go back.

### Trimming it

1. Click **✂ Trim border** (or press **T**). The proposed trim appears, for example "Proposed trim: left 16 px · confidence 0.95". It may say **No border found**, or "Possible border — not sure enough to trim. Use Adjust to trim it by hand."
2. Choose one of these:
   * **Accept**: apply the trim as shown.
   * **Adjust**: drag each edge to set how much to trim yourself, then click **Apply trim**. The frame still keeps its shape and size.
   * **Don't trim**: leave the frame as it is and clear its badge. This is only offered on **Border suggested** and **Check border** frames.
   * **Cancel** (or **Esc**): close the trim without changing anything.

![Trimming it](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/7d487bbb-c0c6-4e7b-b949-915bc301e962.png)

### Undoing a trim

On a trimmed frame:

* **Show original** (press **O**, or hold **Space**) shows the untrimmed picture with the removed area shaded.
* **Revert to original** (**Shift+T**) puts the frame back exactly as it was scanned.
* **✂ Trim border** reopens the trim so you can adjust it.

* Note: If a frame has been enhanced with Perfectly Clear, revert Perfectly Clear first (**↺ Revert PC**), then trim, then enhance again.
* Note: Trimming is available until the roll is uploaded. After that, the frame is final.

---

## Frame viewer keys

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **[** / **]** | Previous / next frame |
| **←** / **→** (or **L** / **R**) | Rotate left / right |
| **T** | Trim border |
| **Shift+T** | Revert to original |
| **O**, or hold **Space** | Show original (trimmed frames) |
| **M** | Magnifier: 100% pixels under the mouse |
| **P** / **Shift+P** | Enhance with Perfectly Clear / revert it |
| **G** | Flag menu |
| **F** | Quick-flag as wrong rotation |
| **Esc** | Close (or cancel an open trim) |

Hover over any toolbar button to see its key.

---

## Good to know

* **Thin borders only.** Automatic trimming only ever takes a thin strip off an edge. A wider border can still be trimmed by hand with **Adjust**.
* **Nothing is lost.** The untrimmed original stays on this PC until the roll is cleared by your normal clean-up, and it is never uploaded.
* **Larger files.** Trimmed JPEGs are saved at full quality, so expect them to be bigger than the scanner's originals.
* **Your decision sticks.** Once you choose **Don't trim** or **Revert to original**, that frame won't be flagged or trimmed again.
